answer: Seats are bound to one numbered beacon tower on a named ridge, not to a wallet. Each epoch the keeper climbs there at an hour drawn from fog and battery voltage, strikes the lamp by hand, and uploads the light-pulse arrival gaps logged by the two neighbouring towers. Mist, wet stone and a sagging wick shift those gaps, and each tower pair cross-signs the other, so a fake seat needs two colluding real keepers. Every extra identity therefore demands staffed towers on both sides. A fable seals it: the keeper recites the local tale aloud, and only years of residence keep its details straight.
